appraisal_events.evidence: «Vite, appelez-moi Cyprien, une table pour M. le marquis de Saint-Loup», s'écriait le patron, pour qui Robert n'était pas seulement un grand seigneur jouissant d'un véritable prestige, même aux yeux du prince de Foix, mais un client qui menait la vie à grandes guides; «je vis le patron s'infléchir en courbettes, les maîtres d'hôtel accourir au grand complet, ce qui fit tourner les yeux à tous les clients».
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup's entrance instantly reorganizes the restaurant around him — bowing patron, the full staff summoned, every eye turning, a door condemned on his order — and the narrator underwrites the display by asserting a «véritable prestige» that holds even by the standard of the prince de Foix, whom the room had just been flattering. The mercenary note (he spends heavily here) colors the patron's motive but is added to, not substituted for, the genuine seigneurial standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: «une familiarité dont j'étais seul exclu»; puis «Il me donnait des marques de respect excessives pour que j'oubliasse qu'elles n'avaient pas commencé dès mon arrivée, mais seulement après celle de Saint-Loup», avec «de petits sourires où semblait se déclarer une sympathie toute personnelle».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator passes from being the single person excluded from the room's shipwreck-survivor camaraderie to being the one for whom tables are moved, a door sealed, and excessive deference performed — standing borrowed entirely from Saint-Loup's visible friendship. The narrator ironizes the patron's belated, calculated zeal and his counterfeit «sympathie toute personnelle», but the local inclusion he gains is nonetheless real and is the passage's closing movement.

status_effects.explanation: Within the scene Saint-Loup becomes the locally dominant figure of prestige: the establishment mobilizes for him, his commands are executed with fearful zeal, and his standing is explicitly ranked as real even in the eyes of the prince de Foix, the room's previous object of deference.

He moves from «seul exclu» to conspicuous inclusion — publicly claimed by Saint-Loup with intimate warmth and then courted by the staff — a clear local reversal even though the deference is derivative and exposed as insincere.

ambiguities: The opening «quatre gigolos» paragraph runs counter to the dominant movement: the narrator formally denies the rumors of intimacy «en ce qui concernait Saint-Loup», then reports that «plus tard, si l'on apprit que ces bruits étaient vrais pour tous les quatre», retroactively including him. This prospective discredit-by-association is narrated with amused detachment and is not part of the restaurant scene's local dynamics, so it is not scored, but it qualifies any purely positive reading of Saint-Loup here.
